title: Unfair trade practices, discipline, fraud and privacy
summary: Dana's first agency year: Michigan's banned sales tricks, the $50 gift, premium money, license discipline and fines, fraud, and privacy notices.
objectives: Tell twisting, rebating and misrepresentation apart, plus other unfair practices
Apply the $50 gift limit, rebating penalties and fiduciary rules for premiums
Recall discipline tiers, fines, and fraud penalties and reporting immunity
Use PAPER to remember Michigan's privacy notice rules

scenes.title: Dana and the agent across the street
scenes.subtitle: Michigan's banned sales tricks, the $50 gift, premium money, license discipline, fines, fraud and privacy

beats.text: It's Dana's first year with her own Grand Rapids agency. Business is slow, and Vic, across Main Street, plays dirty.
beats.say: It's Dana's first year with her own Grand Rapids agency. Business is slow, and Vic, across Main Street, plays dirty.

beats.text: I'll beat him by the book. Watch me.
beats.say: I'll beat him by the book. Watch me.

scenes.title: Vic's three tricks
scenes.src: MCL 500.2005a(a) (twisting); MCL 500.2066(1) (rebating); MCL 500.2005 (misrepresentation); confusion pair cp_personal-15

beats.text: The exam loves to mix up Vic's three tricks. Watch.
beats.say: The exam loves to mix up Vic's three tricks. Watch.

beats.text: One: to get Tony to switch, Vic's comparison promises he'll save $20 but hides the new deductibles. A knowingly misleading representation or incomplete comparison, to get a policy dropped or replaced, is twisting.
beats.say: One: to get Tony to switch, Vic's comparison promises he'll save twenty dollars but hides the new deductibles. A knowingly misleading representation or incomplete comparison, to get a policy dropped or replaced, is twisting.

beats.text: Two: cash back. Vic offers Rosa $200 back. Giving back premium or commission, or anything of value the policy doesn't specify, is rebating.
beats.say: Two: cash back. Vic offers Rosa two hundred dollars back. Giving back premium or commission, or anything of value the policy doesn't specify, is rebating.

beats.text: Three: a lie. Vic claims his insurer never loses money. Misstating a policy's terms or benefits, or an insurer's financial condition, is misrepresentation.
beats.say: Three: a lie. Vic claims his insurer never loses money. Misstating a policy's terms or benefits, or an insurer's financial condition, is misrepresentation.

beats.text: The tell: switch, twisting. Payback, rebating. False picture, misrepresentation.
beats.say: The tell: switch, twisting. Payback, rebating. False picture, misrepresentation.

scenes.title: Switch, payback or false picture?
scenes.src: Confusion pair cp_personal-15 (drills); MCL 500.2005; MCL 500.2005a(a); MCL 500.2066(1); MCL 500.2070

cards.text: An agent offers to send a prospect $200 of his commission if she buys a homeowners policy.
cards.why: Returning part of the commission is a rebate: valuable consideration not specified in the policy.

cards.text: To get Rosa to drop her auto policy, an agent's comparison hides the new policy's much higher deductibles.
cards.why: An incomplete comparison used to get someone to drop one policy and take another is twisting.

cards.text: An agent tells Sam his homeowners policy covers flood damage. It excludes flood.
cards.why: Misrepresentation: it misstates the policy's terms and benefits. No switch of policies is involved.

cards.text: Tony knowingly accepts a gift card worth $300 for buying a policy.
cards.why: $300 of value the policy doesn't specify is a rebate. Tony knowingly took it, so his insurance is reduced in proportion.

cards.text: An agent falsely tells a prospect his insurer has billions in surplus and never had a losing year.
cards.why: Misrepresenting an insurer's financial condition is a listed misrepresentation.

beats.text: Your turn: which trick is it?
beats.say: Your turn: which trick is it?

reveal.text: Watch out: twisting is a misrepresentation aimed at a switch. Cash to switch, with nothing misleading said, is rebating, not twisting.
reveal.say: Watch out: twisting is a misrepresentation aimed at a switch. Cash to switch, with nothing misleading said, is rebating, not twisting.

scenes.title: The cherry basket rule
scenes.src: MCL 500.2024b (am. 2018 PA 542); MCL 500.2066(1); memory hook mn_reg-18
scenes.plain: In P&C, a small thank-you gift is fine: merchandise costing the insurer $50 or less per calendar year. Cash back is not.
scenes.example: A Traverse City cherry basket is a thank-you; a cash-back envelope is a rebate. Keep the basket at $50 a year.
scenes.exam: Watch out: $50 per calendar year, measured by cost to the insurer, for merchandise. Older materials may show another figure.

beats.text: Is every gift a rebate? No. Michigan P&C has a gift limit: merchandise costing the insurer $50 or less per calendar year is allowed. Cash back is not.
beats.say: Is every gift a rebate? No. Michigan P and C has a gift limit: merchandise costing the insurer fifty dollars or less per calendar year is allowed. Cash back is not.

beats.text: The hook: a Traverse City cherry basket is a thank-you; a cash-back envelope is a rebate. Keep the basket at $50 a year.
beats.say: The hook: a Traverse City cherry basket is a thank-you; a cash-back envelope is a rebate. Keep the basket at fifty dollars a year.

beats.text: Older materials may show another figure; $50 is the 2018 amendment.
beats.say: Older materials may show another figure; fifty dollars is the twenty eighteen amendment.

draw.text: Vic will send me $200. Can you match it?

beats.text: Vic will send me $200 of his commission to switch. Can you match it?
beats.say: Vic will send me two hundred dollars of his commission to switch. Can you match it?

options.label: Match it: send Sam $200 of her commission
options.fail: Cash to stay or to switch is rebating, not twisting: license revoked, no new one for 1 year, plus a misdemeanor fine up to $100 per violation.

beats.text: Dana sends the cash. That's rebating. On proof of it, Michigan revokes her license, with no new one for a year.
beats.say: Dana sends the cash. That's rebating. On proof of it, Michigan revokes her license, with no new one for a year.

options.label: Skip the cash: give Sam a basket costing $90
options.fail: The gift exception covers only merchandise costing the insurer $50 or less per calendar year. A basket costing $90 is a rebate.

beats.text: A basket costing $90? That's over $50, so it's still an illegal rebate.
beats.say: A basket costing ninety dollars? That's over fifty dollars, so it's still an illegal rebate.

options.label: Say no, and give Sam a basket costing $40
options.win: Merchandise costing the insurer $50 or less per calendar year is allowed. This basket costs $40 and is Sam's only gift this year.

beats.text: Cherries? Fine, I'm staying.
beats.say: Cherries? Fine, I'm staying.

beats.text: A legal thank-you: $50 or less a year.
beats.say: A legal thank-you: fifty dollars or less a year.

reveal.text: A rebating agent's license is revoked, with no new one for a year. A customer who knowingly takes a rebate gets coverage reduced in proportion.
reveal.say: A rebating agent's license is revoked, with no new one for a year. A customer who knowingly takes a rebate gets coverage reduced in proportion.

reveal.text: Rebating is also a misdemeanor for both, with a fine up to $100. For the agent, that's per violation.
reveal.say: Rebating is also a misdemeanor for both, with a fine up to one hundred dollars. For the agent, that's per violation.

draw.text: We'll never write for Dana's customers!

spots.label: Defamation
spots.text: De-FAME: a billboard on I-94 falsely shouting 'Rival Mutual is going broke!' to steal its customers. Spoken attacks count too.

spots.label: False advertising
spots.text: Vic's ad says 'Michigan's oldest agency!', but he opened last year. Insurance ads and announcements may not be untrue, deceptive or misleading, in any medium.

spots.label: Lender coercion
spots.text: A lender may not make a loan depend on buying insurance through a particular agent or insurer. It may reasonably approve the insurer you pick.

spots.label: Boycott
spots.text: BCI = Bullies Can't Insure: Boycott, Coercion, Intimidation. Insurers agreeing to shun one agency's customers unreasonably restrain its business.

spots.label: Unfair discrimination
spots.text: Grandma's refusal letter gives the reason: a past denial. An insurer may not refuse to insure someone solely because another insurer previously denied her coverage.

beats.text: More trouble in town. Tap each spot to see what Michigan bans.
beats.say: More trouble in town. Tap each spot to see what Michigan bans.

reveal.text: All five are banned in Michigan. Defamation's tell: a false or malicious attack on an insurance business's finances.
reveal.say: All five are banned in Michigan. Defamation's tell: a false or malicious attack on an insurance business's finances.

scenes.title: Premiums are fiduciary money
scenes.plain: Money Dana holds in trust for others. Premiums and return premiums aren't hers: kept apart (segregated), never mixed (commingled) with her own.
scenes.example: Sam's premium goes in Dana's premium account at a federally insured bank, where it may earn interest. Her lunch money stays out.
scenes.exam: Trap: personal checking, even with a ledger, is commingling. Holding a refund for future premiums takes the insured's written OK.

beats.text: In Michigan, premiums Dana collects are fiduciary money: she holds them in trust for others. So are return premiums. They aren't hers, so they're segregated, or kept apart, and never commingled, or mixed, with her own.
beats.say: In Michigan, premiums Dana collects are fiduciary money: she holds them in trust for others. So are return premiums. They aren't hers, so they're segregated, or kept apart, and never commingled, or mixed, with her own.

beats.text: Sam's premium goes in Dana's premium account, a separate account at a federally insured bank, where it may earn interest. Her lunch money stays out.
beats.say: Sam's premium goes in Dana's premium account, a separate account at a federally insured bank, where it may earn interest. Her lunch money stays out.

beats.text: Her own money goes in only to open the account and to pay or avoid bank charges. Late turnover is prima facie evidence of a violation.
beats.say: Her own money goes in only to open the account and to pay or avoid bank charges. Late turnover is prima facie evidence of a violation.

beats.text: Here's the trap: putting premiums in personal checking, even with a ledger, is commingling. And holding a refund for future premiums takes the insured's written OK.
beats.say: Here's the trap: putting premiums in personal checking, even with a ledger, is commingling. And holding a refund for future premiums takes the insured's written OK.

scenes.title: Dana's call: Sam's $120 refund
scenes.ask: What does Dana do with it?

draw.text: Hold it for his next bill?

beats.text: The insurer sends Dana $120 for Sam: a return premium. She could put it toward his next bill. What does she do?
beats.say: The insurer sends Dana one hundred twenty dollars for Sam: a return premium. She could put it toward his next bill. What does she do?

options.label: Park it in her own checking for now
options.fail: Return premiums are fiduciary money too: kept in the separate account, never commingled with the agent's own.

beats.text: The refund lands next to Dana's lunch money. Commingled!
beats.say: The refund lands next to Dana's lunch money. Commingled!

options.label: Phone Sam, get a quick OK, then hold it
options.fail: She may hold a return premium for future premiums only with the insured's written authorization. A spoken OK doesn't count.

beats.text: Sure, keep it for my bill!
beats.say: Sure, keep it for my bill!

beats.text: A phone OK isn't written. Not enough.
beats.say: A phone OK isn't written. Not enough.

draw.text: Sure, keep it for my bill!

options.label: Get Sam's written OK, then hold it
options.win: With the insured's written authorization, a return premium may stay in the premium account to pay future premiums.

beats.text: Sam signs. The refund waits in the premium account.
beats.say: Sam signs. The refund waits in the premium account.

reveal.text: Holding a return premium for future premiums takes the insured's written authorization.
reveal.say: Holding a return premium for future premiums takes the insured's written authorization.

scenes.title: Who can get a license?
scenes.term: Shall not issue vs may refuse
scenes.plain: Shall not issue: the director must deny the license. May refuse: the director decides.
scenes.example: The 10-year rearview mirror: a felony still in the mirror means no license. Violent, sex and money felonies are 'closer than they appear'; they never leave the mirror.
scenes.exam: Also shall not issue: forging a name on an insurance document, or knowingly accepting business from an unlicensed person.

draw.text: Violent, sex, money: always in view

beats.text: Dana's hiring. In Michigan, licenses come from the director. Shall not issue: the director must deny one. May refuse: the director decides.
beats.say: Dana's hiring. In Michigan, licenses come from the director. Shall not issue: the director must deny one. May refuse: the director decides.

beats.text: The 10-year rearview mirror: a felony still in the mirror means no license. Violent, sex and money felonies are 'closer than they appear'; they never leave the mirror. Shall not issue: a felony within 10 years before applying, or a violent, sexual or financial felony at any time.
beats.say: The ten-year rearview mirror: a felony still in the mirror means no license. Violent, sex and money felonies are closer than they appear; they never leave the mirror. Shall not issue: a felony within ten years before applying, or a violent, sexual or financial felony at any time.

beats.text: Also shall not issue: forging someone's name on an insurance document, or knowingly accepting business from an unlicensed person.
beats.say: Also shall not issue: forging someone's name on an insurance document, or knowingly accepting business from an unlicensed person.

beats.text: May refuse: false or incomplete application answers, other felonies, a license denied, suspended or revoked in another state, or using notes during the exam.
beats.say: May refuse: false or incomplete application answers, other felonies, a license denied, suspended or revoked in another state, or using notes during the exam.

scenes.title: Sort Dana's job applicants
scenes.src: MCL 500.1239(1)(d),(e),(h),(i); MCL 500.1239(2)(a)-(d); question reg-031; memory hook mn_reg-12

items.text: A felony conviction 6 years before applying
items.why: Any felony within 10 years before applying.
Financial felonies count at any date.

items.text: Forged a customer's name on an application
items.why: Forging a name on an insurance document.

items.text: Knowingly took business from the unlicensed
items.why: Knowingly accepting business from the unlicensed.

items.text: Used notes during the licensing exam
items.why: Notes or reference material during the exam.
Denied, suspended or revoked in another state.

items.text: Gave incomplete answers on the application
A 15-year-old felony, not violent, sexual or financial
items.why: Older felonies of other kinds: may refuse.

beats.text: Your turn: shall not issue, or may refuse?
beats.say: Your turn: shall not issue, or may refuse?

reveal.text: Violent, sexual and money felonies never leave the mirror.
reveal.say: Violent, sexual and money felonies never leave the mirror.

reveal.text: Any of these can also cost a current licensee: probation, suspension, revocation or a fine.
reveal.say: Any of these can also cost a current licensee: probation, suspension, revocation or a fine.

draw.text: max each, knew or reasonably should have known
max each if you knew or should have; cap $50,000 per 6 months

beats.text: After a hearing, Michigan's director issues a cease and desist order and may add fines.
beats.say: After a hearing, Michigan's director issues a cease and desist order and may add fines.

beats.text: Licensing law, in thousands: Oops 1, didn't know. Knew 5, knew or reasonably should have. Those are maximums per violation. Cap 50 per order.
beats.say: Licensing law, in thousands: Oops one, didn't know. Knew five, knew or reasonably should have. Those are maximums per violation. Cap fifty per order.

beats.text: Trade practices law uses the same $1,000 and $5,000. Its caps are ten times those: $10,000 total, or $50,000 per 6 months if you knew or should have.
beats.say: Trade practices law uses the same one thousand dollars and five thousand dollars. Its caps are ten times those: ten thousand dollars total, or fifty thousand dollars per six months if you knew or should have.

beats.text: Defy either order: up to $20,000 each. For a licensing order, that's for knowing violations, capped at $100,000.
beats.say: Defy either order: up to twenty thousand dollars each. For a licensing order, that's for knowing violations, capped at one hundred thousand dollars.

scenes.title: Tony's call: the cracked oven
scenes.src: MCL 500.4503; MCL 500.4511(1),(2); memory hook mn_reg-19; questions reg-052, reg-053

beats.text: Detroit, January. Tony's pizza oven cracks, and he files an insurance claim. The real repair estimate: $2,000.
beats.say: Detroit, January. Tony's pizza oven cracks, and he files an insurance claim. The real repair estimate: two thousand dollars.

beats.text: $6,000 sounds better. Who'd know?
beats.say: Six thousand dollars sounds better. Who'd know?

options.label: Inflate it to $6,000 and send it in himself
options.fail: Knowingly presenting false material information on a claim, to defraud, is a felony: up to 4 years and/or $50,000, plus restitution.

beats.text: Tony sends in the doctored estimate: under Michigan law, a felony. Up to four years, a fine up to $50,000, or both, plus paying it back.
beats.say: Tony sends in the doctored estimate: under Michigan law, a felony. Up to four years, a fine up to fifty thousand dollars, or both, plus paying it back.

options.label: Call his cousin to help fake a break-in
options.fail: Agreeing or conspiring to commit insurance fraud is its own felony: up to 10 years and/or $50,000, plus restitution.

beats.text: Tony and his cousin agree to fake a break-in. Agreeing to commit insurance fraud: a felony, up to ten years.
beats.say: Tony and his cousin agree to fake a break-in. Agreeing to commit insurance fraud: a felony, up to ten years.

options.label: Send the real estimate of $2,000
options.win: An honest claim is no crime. Knowingly faking one, alone or with a partner, is a felony.

beats.text: Honest pizza, honest claim.
beats.say: Honest pizza, honest claim.

reveal.text: Solo 4, Squad 10: committing fraud risks 4 years; plotting it with a partner risks 10. Either way, up to $50,000 and you pay it back.
reveal.say: Solo four, Squad ten: committing fraud risks four years; plotting it with a partner risks ten. Either way, up to fifty thousand dollars and you pay it back.

scenes.title: Dana reports a fishy estimate
scenes.src: MCL 500.4501(a),(h),(i); MCL 500.4503; MCL 500.4509(1),(3); question reg-055; memory hook mn_reg-19

draw.text: The clinic pays me per patient I bring in for insurance claims!

spots.label: A 'statement'
spots.text: Under the fraud law, statements include estimates, invoices, bills, proofs of loss, claim forms, medical records and X-rays.

spots.label: Fraudulent insurance act
spots.text: Dana's suspicion: an act done knowingly, with intent to injure, defraud or deceive, like false material information on an application or claim. Not this one.

spots.label: Authorized agency
spots.text: Under the fraud law, 'authorized agency' includes the state police, local police and sheriffs, prosecutors, federal investigators, DIFS and the Department of State.

spots.label: Reporting shield
spots.text: Report suspected fraud without malice, and you are not liable for libel, slander or other torts, unless you know the information is false.

spots.label: Runner, capper or steerer
spots.text: Someone a practitioner pays to bring in clients or patients, to obtain insurance benefits or assert claims. A practitioner's public-media ads don't count.

beats.text: Dana suspects a client's repair estimate was altered, and reports it in good faith to the state police.
beats.say: Dana suspects a client's repair estimate was altered, and reports it in good faith to the state police.

beats.text: It's genuine. The client sues for slander. Is Dana liable? Tap the spots.
beats.say: It's genuine. The client sues for slander. Is Dana liable? Tap the spots.

reveal.text: No: she reported without malice and didn't know it was false.
reveal.say: No: she reported without malice and didn't know it was false.

reveal.text: Also: a runner, capper or steerer is paid by a practitioner to bring in patients for insurance claims.
reveal.say: Also: a runner, capper or steerer is paid by a practitioner to bring in patients for insurance claims.

scenes.title: Privacy notices: think PAPER
scenes.hook: Think PAPER for privacy notices: Personal, At the start, Periodic, Exit, Real copy.
items: Personal: personal, family or household insurance, not business buyers
At the start, then Periodic: at least once in any 12 consecutive months
Exit: opt-out before sharing with nonaffiliated third parties; 30 days from mailing is reasonable
Real copy: in writing, or electronic if agreed; never solely oral, and no office sign

beats.text: Last stop: Michigan's privacy notices. Think PAPER: Personal, At the start, Periodic, Exit, Real copy.
beats.say: Last stop: Michigan's privacy notices. Think PAPER: Personal, At the start, Periodic, Exit, Real copy.

beats.text: Personal: personal, family or household insurance, like Sam's homeowners. Not business buyers, like Tony insuring his pizzeria. At the start: a notice no later than when the customer relationship begins. Periodic: at least once in any 12 consecutive months.
beats.say: Personal: personal, family or household insurance, like Sam's homeowners. Not business buyers, like Tony insuring his pizzeria. At the start: a notice no later than when the customer relationship begins. Periodic: at least once in any twelve consecutive months.

beats.text: Exit: before sharing with a nonaffiliated third party, you generally must offer an opt-out. 30 days from mailing is reasonable.
beats.say: Exit: before sharing with a nonaffiliated third party, you generally must offer an opt-out. Thirty days from mailing is reasonable.

beats.text: Real copy: in writing, or electronically if the customer agrees. Never solely oral, and an office sign doesn't count.
beats.say: Real copy: in writing, or electronically if the customer agrees. Never solely oral, and an office sign doesn't count.

scenes.q: Which is NOT an acceptable way for Dana to deliver a required privacy notice?
choices: Mailing a printed copy to the customer
Posting it on a sign in her office lobby
Posting it online for an online customer who must acknowledge receipt
scenes.why: Notices go in writing, or electronically if the consumer agrees: by hand, by mail, or on a website with required acknowledgment. An office sign doesn't count.

beats.text: Quick check: which delivery doesn't count? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Quick check: which delivery doesn't count? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: The office sign. Signs and general advertising don't count. Mail, hand delivery, or a website notice the online customer must acknowledge all work.
reveal.say: The office sign. Signs and general advertising don't count. Mail, hand delivery, or a website notice the online customer must acknowledge all work.

scenes.title: Recap
items: Twisting switches, rebating pays back, misrepresentation misstates
P&C gift: merchandise costing the insurer $50 or less a calendar year
Premiums are fiduciary money: segregated, never commingled
Fraud: up to 4 years solo, 10 with a partner; up to $50,000 either way
Privacy: PAPER; 30 days to opt out is reasonable; never solely oral

beats.text: What a year! Twisting switches, rebating pays back, misrepresentation misstates. A P&C gift? Merchandise costing the insurer $50 or less a calendar year. Premiums are fiduciary money: segregated, never commingled.
beats.say: What a year! Twisting switches, rebating pays back, misrepresentation misstates. A P and C gift? Merchandise costing the insurer fifty dollars or less a calendar year. Premiums are fiduciary money: segregated, never commingled.

beats.text: Fraud: up to 4 years solo, 10 with a partner, and up to $50,000 either way. Privacy: think PAPER. 30 days to opt out is reasonable, and notices are never solely oral.
beats.say: Fraud: up to four years solo, ten with a partner, and up to fifty thousand dollars either way. Privacy: think PAPER. Thirty days to opt out is reasonable, and notices are never solely oral.

beats.say: And Vic got caught rebating. No new license for a year!
